$comment: Project-layer review rules for this repository, read by code-audit-rigor's /review-branch through plugins/code-audit-rigor/scripts/resolve-rules.cjs. Layers: this file → the user's ~/.claude/review-rules/manifest.json → the plugin's built-in rules/manifest.json; within a layer the first matching glob wins, and a file no entry here matches goes on to the user layer and then to the built-in risk heuristics. Only `risk` is set. Deep is everything that executes with the user's permissions or decides what the review itself does: plugin scripts, hooks and validators, every other plugin code file (the plugin-edit hook bash-runs tests/*.test.sh, the fixture runner spawns validators outside validators/), the repo-level scripts, the hook wiring and sandbox denyWrite list in .claude/settings.json, stdio MCP server definitions, the shipped rule packs and the schemas the validators enforce, and this manifest. Standard, listed first so later globs cannot catch them: test fixtures (data, never executed). docs/ is prose nothing executes. Under --base (what /review-branch passes) this file is read from the base revision: a change to it takes effect from the first PR after it merges, never on the PR that makes it.

risk.why: the review policy itself: under --base the base copy of this list decides the tier of the PR that changes it
hook wiring and sandbox denyWrite list; the PostToolUse command runs outside the sandbox with the user's permissions (CONTRIBUTING 6.5)
stdio MCP server command, spawned outside the sandbox with the user's permissions
test fixtures: data the validators read under test, never executed; listed before the code and schema entries so a fixture named like a script or a schema stays standard
review tooling: parses untrusted branch content or runs as a hook
plugin code wherever it lives: the plugin-edit hook bash-runs every tests/*.test.sh and the fixture runner spawns validators outside validators/ (security-audit's vendored validate-findings.cjs)
shipped rule packs: the built-in risk heuristics and the Review focus / Do NOT report lists every installing user's reviewer reads
validator contracts (*.schema.json, report-schema.json): loosening a schema makes a validator accept what it exists to refuse
repo-level automation: fixture runner and the plugin-edit hook
design notes and plans: prose that nothing executes; the built-in payment heuristic matches the word ledger in docs/scope-ledger-*.md
